questions.text:
Directions: In the sentence given below, one/some parts have errors and others are correct. Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is 'No error' as your answer.

Bellicose assertions by China along the LAC, Beijing’s brazen anti-India partisanship/ (A) in international forums and the ongoing attempt to isolate New Delhi in/ (B) its own sub-continental sphere of influence is a byproduct/ (C) of the hubris that has swept on the Chinese Communist Party./ (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "on" in part D.
  • The correct phrasal verb is "swept over," which is used to describe a powerful emotion, quality, or idea spreading through or affecting someone or something.
  • In this context, "hubris" (excessive pride) is the quality that has powerfully affected the Chinese Communist Party, requiring the use of "over" instead of "on."
  • Thus, the error is located in part D of the sentence, making Option A (Only D) the correct answer.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "Bellicose assertions by China along the LAC, Beijing’s brazen anti-India partisanship in international forums and the ongoing attempt to isolate New Delhi in its own sub-continental sphere of influence is a byproduct of the hubris that has swept over the Chinese Communist Party."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "Bellicose assertions... partisanship" – This part correctly introduces the plural and singular subjects of the sentence.
  • B: "in international forums... isolate New Delhi in" – This part is grammatically sound and maintains proper prepositional usage and parallel structure.
  • C: "its own sub-continental sphere of influence is a byproduct" – This part is acceptable as the verb "is" treats the collective actions mentioned previously as a singular unified phenomenon.
  • No error – This would be the correct option if the sentence were grammatically perfect, but the error in part D prevents this.

Police also charged three men (a)/ and a woman from Montgomery with (b)/ felony criminal mischiefs for toppling (c)/ the statue outside Lee High. (d)/ no error

options.text: and a woman from Montgomery with

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The primary error in the sentence is the use of the plural noun "mischiefs" in part C.
  • The word "mischief" is an uncountable noun when it refers to playful misbehaviour or, in legal terms, the crime of damaging property ("criminal mischief").
  • Uncountable nouns do not typically have a plural form. Therefore, "mischiefs" should be replaced with "mischief" to be grammatically correct.
  • Thus, the error is located in part C of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "Police also charged three men and a woman from Montgomery with felony criminal mischief for toppling the statue outside Lee High."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "Police also charged three men" – This part is correct; "police" is treated as a plural noun and the verb tense is consistent.
  • B: "and a woman from Montgomery with" – This part is correct; the preposition "with" is the standard accompaniment for the verb "charged" (charged someone with something).
  • D: "the statue outside Lee High." – This part is correct; "outside" is used correctly as a preposition of place.
  • no error – This option is incorrect because a grammatical error exists in the usage of the noun "mischiefs."

There isn't a ton of wildlife to see living in South Korea (a)/ so Ducky has been absolutely living it up (b)/ with all the birds, squirrels, chipmunks, raccoons (c)/ and deers that regularly wander by the windows! (d)/ no error

options.text: There isn't a ton of wildlife to see living in a South Korean
so Ducky has been absolutely living it up
with all the birds, squirrels, chipmunks, raccoons
and deers that regularly wander by the windows!

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary error in the sentence is the use of the word "deers" in part D.
  • In English, certain nouns have the same form for both singular and plural. "Deer" is one of these irregular nouns.
  • The correct plural form should be "deer," regardless of whether it refers to one or multiple animals.
  • Thus, the error is located in part D of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "There isn't a ton of wildlife to see living in South Korea so Ducky has been absolutely living it up with all the birds, squirrels, chipmunks, raccoons and deer that regularly wander by the windows!"
 
Additional Information
  • A: "There isn't a ton of wildlife to see living in South Korea" – This part is grammatically correct; "wildlife" is an uncountable noun used with a singular verb.
  • B: "so Ducky has been absolutely living it up" – This part correctly uses the present perfect continuous tense and the idiom "living it up."
  • C: "with all the birds, squirrels, chipmunks, raccoons" – This part is a correctly formatted list of plural countable nouns.
  • Other examples of nouns that remain the same in plural include sheep, fish, and series.

questions.text:
Directions: In the sentence given below, one/some parts have errors and others are correct. Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is 'No error' as your answer.

The IMF yesterday lowered its quarterly forecast of India’s economic growth for 2020-21/ (A) from -4.5%, to about 1.9% it had anticipated in April. In just three months,/ (B) India’s growth forecast has been lowered by 6.4 percentage points. Along with/ (C) a reduction in India’s forecast, IMF has lowered the forecast for the rest of the world./ (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The primary error in the sentence is the logical reversal of the prepositions "from" and "to" in part B.
  • The verb "lowered" indicates a reduction, which implies moving from a higher value to a lower one.
  • Since 1.9% was the previous figure (anticipated in April) and -4.5% is the new, lower figure, the correct phrasing must be "to -4.5% from about 1.9%."
  • Thus, the error is located in part B of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "The IMF yesterday lowered its quarterly forecast of India’s economic growth for 2020-21 to -4.5%, from about 1.9% it had anticipated in April. In just three months, India’s growth forecast has been lowered by 6.4 percentage points."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "The IMF yesterday lowered its quarterly forecast of India’s economic growth for 2020-21/" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • C: "India’s growth forecast has been lowered by 6.4 percentage points. Along with/" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • D: "a reduction in India’s forecast, IMF has lowered the forecast for the rest of the world./" – While "the" is missing before "IMF," the logical error in part B is the primary focus of this identification task.
  • No error – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is a significant logical error in part B.

Directions: In the sentence given below, one/some parts have errors and others are correct. Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is 'No error' as your answer.

The rath yatra was a non-justiciable issue in which the local/ (A) administration was required to apply its mind and eke on/ (B) a socio-political consensus. Judiciary needs to be/ (C) wary by governments shifting the burden of executive decisions to it./ (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence contains errors in Part B and Part D.
  • In Part B, the phrasal verb "eke on" is incorrect. The correct idiom is "eke out," which means to manage to produce or supplement something with great effort (e.g., "eke out a consensus").
  • In Part D, the preposition "by" used after the adjective "wary" is incorrect. The standard preposition to use with "wary" is "of" (e.g., "wary of something").
  • Thus, the errors are located in parts B and D.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: "The rath yatra was a non-justiciable issue in which the local administration was required to apply its mind and eke out a socio-political consensus. Judiciary needs to be wary of governments shifting the burden of executive decisions to it."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "The rath yatra was a non-justiciable issue in which the local" – This part is grammatically correct. "Non-justiciable" refers to an issue not capable of being decided by legal principles or by a court of justice.
  • C: "a socio-political consensus. Judiciary needs to be" – While "The" is typically used before "judiciary" in formal writing, in the context of these specific error-spotting options, the errors in B and D (idiom and preposition) are the primary focus.
  • Eke out: To make something last longer or to obtain/create something with difficulty.
  • Wary of: Feeling or showing caution about possible dangers or problems.

With their aid, he should be able (a)/ to adapt himself selectively to his culture, (b)/ rejecting its evils, stupidities and irrelevances, (c)/ gratefully accepting all its treasures of accumulated knowledges. (d)/ no error

options.text: With their aid, he should be able
to adapt himself selectively to his culture,
rejecting its evils, stupidities and irrelevances,
gratefully accepting all its treasures of accumulated knowledges.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The primary error in the sentence lies in the use of the word "knowledges" in part D.
  • The word "knowledge" is an uncountable noun (mass noun), which means it typically does not have a plural form.
  • In standard English, the term "knowledge" is used for both general and specific accumulated information, and adding an "s" is grammatically incorrect.
  • Thus, the error is located in part D of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "With their aid, he should be able to adapt himself selectively to his culture, rejecting its evils, stupidities and irrelevances, gratefully accepting all its treasures of accumulated knowledge."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "With their aid, he should be able" – This part is grammatically correct as it sets up the capability of the subject.
  • B: "to adapt himself selectively to his culture," – This part is correct; "adapt" is used with the reflexive pronoun "himself" and the correct preposition "to."
  • C: "rejecting its evils, stupidities and irrelevances," – This part is correct; these specific nouns are used here to describe plural instances of negative traits.
  • No error – This option is incorrect because part D contains a clear grammatical error regarding noun countability.

You do not know the relief of brushing away a fly(A)/ that has bitten you, or the delight of eating(B)/ delicious food, or the satisfaction of(C)/ drawing a long breath of fresh, pure air.(D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 5.
 
Key Points
  • The provided sentence is grammatically sound and does not contain any errors in its parts.
  • The sentence follows a parallel structure: "the relief of brushing...", "the delight of eating...", and "the satisfaction of drawing...".
  • Each part (A, B, C, and D) uses correct prepositions, articles, and verb forms within their respective contexts.
  • Since all parts of the sentence are correct, the choice is No error.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 5.
 
Correct Sentence: "You do not know the relief of brushing away a fly that has bitten you, or the delight of eating delicious food, or the satisfaction of drawing a long breath of fresh, pure air."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "You do not know the relief of brushing away a fly" – Correct subject-verb agreement and prepositional usage.
  • B: "that has bitten you, or the delight of eating" – The relative clause and the start of the parallel list are correct.
  • C: "delicious food, or the satisfaction of" – Maintains the list structure and uses appropriate nouns.
  • D: "drawing a long breath of fresh, pure air." – Correct gerund usage and adjective placement.

questions.text:
Directions: In the sentence given below, one/some parts have errors and others are correct. Find out which part has an error and mark it as your answer. If there is 'No error' as your answer.

The state of the job market in India needs some time to heal. As per a recent study done by/ (A) Knowledgetics Research on Employability Outlook; around 17.6% companies have been/ (B) experiencing shrinking business opportunities, while 34.1% are laying of/ (C) people and 37.4% have put a stop off hiring./ (D)
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The first error occurs in part C with the phrase "laying of." The correct phrasal verb is "laying off," which means to dismiss employees from their jobs.
  • The second error is in part D within the phrase "put a stop off." The correct idiomatic expression is "put a stop to," which means to cause something to end or to prevent it from continuing.
  • Both errors involve the incorrect use of prepositions in standard English expressions.
  • Thus, the errors are located in parts C and D of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "The state of the job market in India needs some time to heal. As per a recent study done by Knowledgetics Research on Employability Outlook; around 17.6% companies have been experiencing shrinking business opportunities, while 34.1% are laying off people and 37.4% have put a stop to hiring."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "As per a recent study done by" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.
  • B: "Knowledgetics Research on Employability Outlook; around 17.6% companies have been" – While formal writing usually requires "of" after a percentage, it is often omitted in business contexts; however, parts C and D contain more fundamental grammatical errors.
  • No error – This option is incorrect because there are clear grammatical mistakes in parts C and D.

In the second year, students (a)/ shadow training officers, before (b)/ returning full time for a third year focused (c)/ on investigations and completing a theses paper. (d)/ no error

options.text: returning full time for a third year focused

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • The error lies in part (d) of the sentence.
  • The primary issue is the use of the plural noun "theses" following the singular indefinite article "a."
  • "Theses" is the plural form of "thesis." Grammatically, the article "a" must be followed by a singular countable noun.
  • The correct phrase should be "a thesis paper" to maintain grammatical agreement.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "In the second year, students shadow training officers, before returning full time for a third year focused on investigations and completing a thesis paper."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "In the second year, students" – This part is grammatically correct as it correctly sets the time context and identifies the subject.
  • B: "shadow training officers, before" – This part is correct; "shadow" is used here as a verb meaning to follow and observe.
  • C: "returning full time for a third year focused" – This part is grammatically correct, describing the duration and nature of the study.
  • E: "No error" – This is incorrect because there is a clear noun-number agreement error in part D.

The police have said that the man, (a)/ who was not identified, was arrested (b)/ and booked into San Mateo County (c)/ Jail on suspicion of commercial burglary. (d)/ no error

options.text: The police have said that the man,
who was not identified, was arrested
and booked into San Mateo County
Jail on suspicion of commercial burglary

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 5.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence provided is grammatically sound and does not contain any errors in its structure, spelling, or punctuation.
  • The noun "police" is a collective noun that is treated as plural, so the use of the plural verb "have" is correct.
  • The non-restrictive relative clause "who was not identified" is correctly set off by commas and uses the singular verb "was" to agree with "the man."
  • The phrase "on suspicion of" is the standard idiomatic expression used in legal and law enforcement contexts.
  • Thus, there is no error in any part of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 5.
 
Correct Sentence: "The police have said that the man, who was not identified, was arrested and booked into San Mateo County Jail on suspicion of commercial burglary."
 
Additional Information
  • A: "The police have said that the man," – This part is correct; "police" always takes a plural verb.
  • B: "who was not identified, was arrested" – This part is correct; it uses proper punctuation for a non-essential clause and correct passive voice.
  • C: "and booked into San Mateo County" – This part is correct; "booked into" is the appropriate phrasal verb for entering a suspect into a facility.
  • D: "Jail on suspicion of commercial burglary." – This part is correct; the proper noun is capitalized and the prepositional phrase is used accurately.
  • no error – This is the correct choice as the sentence adheres to all grammatical rules.
